<h3 align="center">Castaway: menu disk 1992. One title on it, and it runs for ten hours.</h3>

<p align="center">
  <b>Ten hours, one palm, no hurry.</b><br>
  She sits on a very small island and nods to her headphones. Every so often something happens. Then she nods some more.
</p>

**Castaway** *(working title)* is a stationary-frame lo-fi video for YouTube, in the spirit of the ten-hour lofi streams: a young woman alone on a tiny island with one tall palm, a raft and a lot of time. She mostly idles. Every so often a message in a bottle washes straight back, a delivery drone lowers a parcel that turns out to be another pair of headphones, or a coconut lands on a hermit crab and the crab walks off wearing it. It is an unofficial remake inspired by the small-island routines and visual comedy of *Johnny Castaway*, the 1992 desert-island screensaver, repainted in a sunny, hand-painted coastal anime look: 16:9, 1080p, 30 fps, and always daytime.

More than 90 activities sit on four timers, from every few minutes to once in a few hours, and every one of them starts on the next bar of the music, so the gags land on the beat. Every sound is synthesized from code: no samples, no recordings.

<pre>
                  THE LEEWARD LOT PRESENT: MENU DISK 1992, SIDE A

  1...WATCH HER WAIT: LIVE PREVIEW, MP4 EXPORT .............. <a href="tools/serve.py">tools/serve.py</a>
  2...TEN-HOUR SIM: CHECK THE SCHEDULE, RUN IT ........... <a href="tools/schedule.py">tools/schedule.py</a>
  3...SYNTH: EVERY SOUND, FROM CODE .................... <a href="tools/make_audio.py">tools/make_audio.py</a>
  4...DEV REEL: ONE OF EVERYTHING, WITH A HUD ......... <a href="tools/render_demo.py">tools/render_demo.py</a>
  5...THE SCHEDULE ITSELF .................................. <a href="activities.toml">activities.toml</a>
  6...THE RENDERER ITSELF ................................... <a href="web/index.html">web/index.html</a>

  0.......TOGGLE 50/60 HZ: IT RENDERS AT 30 FPS. IT ALWAYS DID.
  SPACE...READ DOC FILE .......................................... <a href="MUSING.md">MUSING.md</a>
  M.......CHANGE MUSIC: THERE IS ONE TUNE. IT HAS BEEN CHOSEN FOR YOU.
</pre>

To load, from the project root:

```sh
python tools/serve.py
# then open http://127.0.0.1:8765/
```

The page plays a live preview and exports a YouTube-ready MP4. In development: no video has been published yet, so for now the only way to watch her wait is to run it.

<details>
<summary><b>SPACE</b>: read doc file (what happens, and how often)</summary>

```text
 ======================================================================
  CASTAWAY.DOC                                   MENU DISK 1992, SIDE A
 ======================================================================

  THE TIMERS        GOES OFF EVERY      IN A TYPICAL TEN-HOUR RUN
  REGULAR ......... 2 to 5 minutes .... about 155
  OCCASIONAL ...... 12 to 25 minutes .. about 30
  RARE ............ 30 to 60 minutes .. about 13
  SUPER RARE ...... 3 to 6 hours ...... about 2, never more than 3
  FOLLOW-UPS ...... only ever after something else
  IDLE ............ the other two thirds of the time. nodding.

  ON THE ISLAND, NOW AND THEN
  * a message in a bottle washes straight back. hours later, a
    different bottle brings a reply
  * a delivery drone lowers a parcel. inside: more headphones
  * a sea turtle swims in and dozes off beside her
  * a grey tabby with a white chest drifts in on a crate, climbs
    the palm, naps, and one day floats off again. it comes back
  * the signal hunt: one bar, at the very top of the palm
  * a shark surfaces in headphones and nods to the beat
  * a tour boat of selfie-takers
  * a coconut falls on a hermit crab. the crab keeps it
  * a bro on an electric hydrofoil gives a shaka and carves off
  * she plants a kumara, and it grows over the course of the video
  * bushcraft: fire by friction, a hammock, a lookout up the palm,
    spear fishing
  * "she could leave any time": she walks out over the water and
    comes back with an iced coffee
  * and in between: a coconut, some fishing, laps of the island, a
    sandcastle for the tide, a wave at the horizon, just in case
```

The counts are the median of 200 simulated runs, as the header of [activities.toml](activities.toml) says. Lanes let things overlap, so the world carries on while she is busy: a ship can sail past behind her while she is deep in a coconut. Every start waits for the next bar of the music, every 3 seconds. The default run is 10:00:00 with seed 1992, which is where this disk gets its number; `python tools/schedule.py` checks the file and simulates a run.

In the banner, the bottle comes back every 24 seconds. In the video it waits its turn on the occasional timer, which it shares with a lot of other things, so in some ten-hour runs it never comes round at all. That is not a bug. That is the island.

</details>

<details>
<summary><b>M</b>: change music (there is one tune, and it is a good sport about it)</summary>

- **All of it is code.** Every sound is synthesized by [tools/make_audio.py](tools/make_audio.py): no samples, no stock loops, no recordings, so no third-party licence applies. More than 150 sound files as of 2026-10-01, and counting.
- **The tune.** A seamless 60-second loop at 80 BPM in F major (ii-V-I-vi), 20 bars of exactly 3 seconds: electric piano, a kalimba lead, soft drums and a bed of vinyl noise. Ten hours is six hundred laps of it, which is why pressing M changes nothing. The script can make more tunes by changing its seed, key, tempo or progression; for now there is the one.
- **The sea.** The ocean ambience is a seamless 60-second loop too. The mix sits at -14 LUFS with true peak at or below -1 dBTP, and levels are adjustable in master and per routine.
- **The honest bit.** Nobody has listened to any of it yet. It has been measured for loudness, clipping and loop seams, which is not the same as being heard.
- **The beat.** One bar is 3 seconds, so the banner keeps time too: the rasters roll one band per bar, the logo sways once per bar, and her head dips on every beat.

</details>

<details>
<summary><b>0</b>: toggle 50/60 Hz (the picture and the machinery)</summary>

- **The picture.** Sunny, hand-painted coastal anime, 16:9, rendered at 1080p and 30 fps. Always daytime: that is a project rule. Hard cuts and stepped movement are the motion defaults. Scene life has 26 entries: shore waves and drifting cloud shadows are built; distant birds, planes with vapour trails, whale pods, dolphins, sailboats, sandpipers, a gecko and a rain shower are planned.
- **The renderer.** A web page, [web/index.html](web/index.html), with live preview and export: it encodes frame-exact H.264 in the browser with WebCodecs (68 to 78 frames a second at 1080p30 in Chrome), and the server mixes the sound and joins the two into an MP4. Plain ES modules, no build step, no npm packages.
- **The dev reel.** `python tools/render_demo.py --dev` renders a reel of every activity with a heads-up display, from the older Python reference renderer.
- **The 50/60 Hz key.** On the ST it switched the screen's refresh rate. Here the answer is 30 fps whichever key you press, and you are encouraged to press none of them.

</details>

The Leeward Lot, its members and everyone it greets in capitals are invented, and so is the disk. The banner is drawn by a script, pixel by pixel: the slab logo, both fonts and the island picture are original, and no group's logo, font or graphics are copied. The style is a nod to the menu screens that UK crews put in front of Atari ST compilation floppies around 1988 to 1991: a key list, rolling rasters, a dithered picture and a big scroller. The only thing on this disk is this project.

</details>
